Representative Kuhn and esteemed colleagues on the Committee on Judiciary, I am Senator
Anne Carney, proudly representing Senate District 29, which includes South Portland, Cape
Elizabeth and part of Scarborough. It is a pleasure to be with you today to introduce LD 250, "An Act Regarding the Disposal of Abandoned Human Remains."
This is a department bill from the Office of Chief Medical Examiner. A representative from their
office will follow me to present more specifics, and I invite you to direct your questions to them.
Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to introduce this bill.

Re: LD 250
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and members of the committee,
I am Lindsey Chasteen, the Office Administrator for the Office of Chief Medical Examiner (OCME). I
am speaking today on LD 250, An Act Regarding the Disposal of Abandoned Human Remains. The
current statute language states the OCME must store identified human remains for a total of 30 days before
the remains are considered abandoned. To be considered abandoned, all efforts must be made to identify a next of kin and there is no next of kin found, or the next of kin has declined the responsibility of making
final arrangements for the deceased.
The OCME, and funeral homes, have seen an increase in the number of abandoned bodies in the past
several years. The OCME takes care of approximately 10 (ten) abandoned bodies each year.
LD 250 looks to lower the number of required storage days when the remains are in the custody of the
OCME to 15 days. This is to align with the current statute language for human remains in the custody of funeral homes (Chap. 707 �2843(2)), and allow the OCME to move decedents along to final arrangements
in a respectful amount of time.
Thank you for your consideration.
